document.title: Expanders Meet Reed-Muller: Easy Instances of Noisy k-XOR

candidate.title: Reed-Muller Codes Efficiently Achieve Capacity for the Binary Erasure Channel
candidate.subtitle: Capacity is known; the rate of convergence to it is not
candidate.one_line: There is a constant gamma such that RM(m,r) recovers from a random Ber(eta) erasure pattern w.p. 1-o(1) whenever eta < eps - 1/M^gamma.
candidate.status_note: Conjecture 14 of the source. That Reed-Muller codes achieve capacity for the BEC is a theorem of Kudekar et al.; what is open is the gap to capacity, i.e. a polynomial rate of convergence. The source needs it to strengthen its refutation of the expansion-implies-hardness conjecture for noisy k-XOR from quasi-polynomially many constraints to polynomially many.
candidate.progress_note: The analogous behaviour is easy for random codes with scaling exponent 2, and polar codes are known to efficiently achieve capacity for binary symmetric channels. For Reed-Muller codes nothing of the kind is known. The source also offers a weaker sufficient form, its Conjecture 16.

parameters.meaning: variables, order and blocklength of RM(m,r)

candidate.why_interesting: A coding-theory question raised in three prior works, given a new consequence: it upgrades a refutation of a widely-held hardness conjecture from quasi-polynomial to polynomial parameters.
candidate.why_clean: One code family, one channel, one inequality. An equivalent purely algebraic form is supplied by the source.
